easy.statement_latex: Determine the maximum number of turning points of a polynomial of degree $12$ such as $p(x) = x^{12} - 1$.
hints: A polynomial of degree $n$ has at most $n - 1$ turning points.
This follows because the derivative of a degree-$n$ polynomial has degree $n - 1$ and therefore at most $n - 1$ real roots.
solution_steps_latex: Apply the turning-point bound: maximum is $n - 1 = 12 - 1 = 11$.
So the graph has at most $11$ turning points.
